mood.headline: Flat to slightly lower open likely as US yields hit 5.1%, oil jumps on Hormuz attacks and CPI tops 6%.
mood.summary: GIFT Nifty was at 25,279 (−22) at 3 AM IST, a touch below Nifty's 25,299 close, pointing to a flat-to-soft start. Overnight the mood worsened: US 10-year yields jumped 12 bps to 5.10%, Wall Street slipped about 0.4% after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned, and Brent rose 3.3% to $95.82 after Iran said four tankers were hit by mines near Hormuz and Houthis attacked Saudi oil sites. At home, October CPI came in at 6.09% (food 8.94%), above RBI's 6% ceiling, so a December rate hike looks more likely — negative for rate-sensitive banks, NBFCs, autos and realty. FPIs have been heavy buyers (₹65,735 cr in November up to Wednesday; Thursday's figure not yet published), which can cushion dips, but the rupee weakened to 94.03 and crude-sensitive stocks (OMCs, paints, aviation) may be under pressure. Expect a range of about 25,150–25,400 with stock-specific moves on results.

news.headline: GIFT Nifty at 25,279 signals a flat-to-soft start
news.summary: GIFT Nifty futures were 22 points lower at 25,279, slightly below Nifty's 25,299 close.
news.why: Points to a quiet start; overnight oil spike and US yields are the main risks.

news.headline: Nifty rises for a third day to 25,299; realty jumps 4.5%, autos and FMCG slip
news.summary: Sensex +32 to 81,911 and Nifty +44 to 25,299 in a volatile session; financials and realty offset selling in IT, FMCG and autos. VIX fell 5.4% to 16.61.
news.why: Index is stuck in a 25,000–25,500 band; breakouts need fresh triggers.

news.headline: India's October CPI rises to 6.09%, breaching RBI's 6% ceiling
news.summary: Retail inflation rose to 6.09% from 5.54%, its highest since October 2024; food inflation hit 8.94% with onion prices up 116%.
news.why: Makes another RBI hike at the 2–4 Dec meeting more likely — negative for banks, NBFCs, realty and autos; bond yields may rise.

news.headline: Rupee weakens 34 paise to 94.03 per dollar
news.summary: The rupee slipped back above 94 as the dollar firmed on Fed hike bets.
news.why: A weaker rupee raises the oil import bill and can slow FII buying; helps IT and pharma exporters.

news.headline: Godrej Industries jumps up to 13% as Temasek invests ₹2,500 cr in Godrej Capital
news.summary: A Temasek affiliate will invest ₹2,500 cr in Godrej Capital, valuing the lending arm at up to ₹28,000 cr.
news.why: Puts a value on the unlisted finance arm and funds its growth; already a big one-day jump.

news.headline: Page Industries falls 12.9% after weak Q2: profit up only 4%
news.summary: Q2 FY27 total income rose 10.9% to ₹1,453 cr but net profit grew just 4% to ₹202.5 cr; stock closed at ₹31,850.
news.why: Shows margin pressure for the Jockey maker; premium valuation leaves little room for misses.

news.headline: Bharat Dynamics falls 6.6% as Q2 profit drops 15%

news.headline: HAL slips 4.3% as Q2 EBITDA margin eases to 22.9%
news.summary: HAL's Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin was 22.9% vs 23.5% a year ago; stock fell to ₹4,736.60.

news.headline: MSCI adds Adani Green, Coforge, LIC and Meesho to India index; PI Industries out

news.headline: FPIs bought ₹12,563 cr on Wednesday; November total ₹65,735 cr

news.headline: Iran says four tankers hit by mines near Hormuz; Houthis strike Saudi oil sites
news.summary: Iran's IRGC said four tankers were hit south of Hormuz while Houthis claimed attacks on a Saudi pipeline station, a Yanbu facility and an Aramco building; Brent jumped 3.3% to $95.82.
news.why: India imports about 85% of its oil; higher crude raises the import bill, inflation and the rupee risk. Hurts OMCs, paints, aviation; helps ONGC and Oil India.

news.headline: US 10-year yield jumps to 5.10% as Fed officials push for more hikes
news.summary: Cleveland Fed's Hammack backed smaller, more frequent hikes; a December hike is fully priced with ~13% odds of 50 bps. The 2-year rose 15 bps to 4.88%.
news.why: Higher US yields pull money out of emerging markets and weaken the rupee; can slow FPI buying in India.

news.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns; Nasdaq dips, AMD and Broadcom rise

news.why: Adds uncertainty to AI spending that drives Indian IT deal flow; watch IT and data-centre names.

news.headline: Wall Street ends lower: S&P 500 −0.35%, Russell 2000 −1.7%
news.summary: US stocks recovered from early losses but closed lower; only energy gained. US VIX rose 6.9% to 18.70.

gold.label: Down ~2.9% overnight
gold.summary: World gold fell 2.9% to $3,885/oz on Thursday, its lowest since October 2025, as US 10-year yields jumped to 5.10% and the dollar index rose to 103.19 (CappNotes). MCX December gold was ~₹1,38,114 (−1.15%) on Thursday afternoon (Kotak Neo), before the bigger overnight drop, so gold ETFs such as GOLDBEES are likely to open lower; the weaker rupee (94.03) cushions only a little. Near-term range about ₹1,35,500–1,40,000; US PPI today and the 9 Dec Fed decision are the next tests.
gold.how: Indian gold ETFs track the domestic gold rate: world gold in dollars × USD/INR, plus import duty. So both world events and the rupee move them.

scenarios.title: Dollar slides again
scenarios.odds: Reversed — dollar firmed after hot CPI on 10 Nov
scenarios.why: The dollar index is near 101.8 and US 10-year yields just under 5%. A renewed dollar slide would lift world gold; a firmer rupee would trim part of the gain for Indian ETFs.
scenarios.line: Dollar up a third day; slide not in sight.

scenarios.title: Fed hikes in December (now near-certain)
scenarios.odds: 25 bp fully priced; ~13% odds of 50 bp (CME via CappNotes, 12 Nov)
scenarios.why: Two Fed members already voted for a hike. A December hike would lift the dollar and yields and weigh on gold; a weaker rupee would cushion part of the fall for Indian ETFs.

scenarios.title: Fed skips December
scenarios.odds: Very unlikely (~0% priced after 10 Nov CPI)
scenarios.why: If inflation data cool, markets would price out the hike; the dollar and yields would fall and gold would rebound.
scenarios.when: Fed 9 Dec; jobs 6 Nov, CPI mid-Nov
scenarios.line: Hot CPI removed most skip bets.

scenarios.title: Gulf conflict widens, oil spikes
scenarios.odds: Rising again — tankers hit near Hormuz (12 Nov)
scenarios.why: Gold usually jumps on war fears, and higher oil weakens the rupee, so Indian gold ETFs gain on both counts. The catch: costly oil also feeds inflation and Fed-hike fears, which has capped gold's rallies recently, so gains can fade.
scenarios.line: Iran says four tankers hit by mines; Brent +3.3% to $95.82, but gold still fell on yields.

scenarios.title: US–Iran de-escalation
scenarios.odds: Less likely — Trump says no deal needed (12 Nov)
scenarios.why: Less war risk removes some safe-haven buying, though cheaper oil also lowers inflation and hike fears, which helps gold. The clearer effect for India is a stronger rupee, which pulls the rupee price of gold down.
scenarios.line: Trump says war 'effectively over'; oil keeps falling.

scenarios.title: Rupee slides past 97
scenarios.why: Every 1% fall in the rupee adds roughly 1% to Indian gold ETF prices even if world gold is flat. Costly oil keeps pressure on the rupee.
scenarios.when: USD/INR 94.03 on 12 Nov vs record low 96.96
scenarios.line: Rupee weakened 34 paise; oil spike adds pressure.

scenarios.title: Rupee recovers
scenarios.odds: Paused — rupee fell to 94.03 on 12 Nov
scenarios.why: The mid-October rupee rally has faded. A renewed recovery, for example on Jio IPO inflows, lower oil or a trade deal, would pressure Indian gold ETFs.
scenarios.when: FPI buying ₹65,735 cr in Nov supports
scenarios.line: Oil crash and FII inflows lift rupee; trims gold ETF gains.

scenarios.title: Stock market sell-off
scenarios.odds: Not under way — US −0.4%, Nifty +0.18% (12 Nov)
scenarios.why: Investors move money into gold when stocks fall. The WGC says weak Indian equities drove gold ETF buying in September. In a severe crash gold can dip briefly as people sell everything to raise cash, then recover.
scenarios.when: Watch Nasdaq after Nvidia CEO exit
scenarios.line: Equity panic usually helps gold, unless funds sell gold to cover losses.

scenarios.title: Central banks keep buying
scenarios.why: China's central bank added 21 tonnes in September, its 23rd straight monthly purchase. Steady official buying tends to limit how far gold falls, though it rarely drives short-term moves.
scenarios.line: China added 21 t in Sept (23rd month); limits downside.

scenarios.title: India cuts import duty
scenarios.why: Indian gold ETFs track the domestic price, which includes customs duty. A duty cut would lower the Indian gold price, and ETF prices, overnight by about the size of the cut, as happened in the July 2024 Budget. A duty hike would do the opposite.
scenarios.line: Domestic gold, and ETFs, drop overnight by about the cut.

guide._all: Each card is a company-specific event from the latest filings and news. Green = likely to support the share, red = likely to pressure it, amber = watch. Today's open may be soft (oil +3.3%, US yields 5.1%, CPI 6.09%), so good news may not lift shares at once. Godrej Industries, Kalyan Jewellers and Bajaj Finance are already up 3%+ — chasing is risky. Defence names (HAL, BDL) fell on results. No client-loss or order-cancellation news found this run. Review-by dates are counted in NSE trading days (24 Nov is a holiday).
guide.Can rise: Positive triggers. A share does not always rise on good news, especially if it ran up before the announcement or the overall market is weak.
guide.Can fall: Negative triggers. Results misses, big investor exits and weak business updates usually hit the share on the day and can weigh for weeks.
guide.Order won: An order matters most when it is big compared with the company's yearly revenue (5–10% or more is significant for smaller companies). Repeat orders and orders in a new area are good signs of future growth. Check the execution period: a 24-month order adds revenue slowly. Being named the only qualified bidder (Goodluck) is a step before an order, not an order itself.
guide.Results: Shares react to results versus expectations, not just growth. Profit growing slower than sales signals squeezed margins, in-line results after a run-up often get sold (Nestle), and guidance for the next quarter can matter more than the quarter itself (Wipro). The earnings call commentary often matters as much as the numbers.
guide.Business update: Monthly sales, pre-sales and festive data give an early read on the quarter before results come out.
guide.Board decision: Board outcomes that usually lift a share: buyback, bonus, stock split, special dividend, demerger or merger that simplifies the group. Ones that can pressure it: big equity fund raise (QIP or rights issue) that adds new shares, large acquisitions that need fresh capital (Aegis), or large related-party deals.
guide.Stake sale: When a promoter or big investor sells in a block deal, the share often falls on the day because the sale is at a discount. If quality institutions buy, it usually recovers within weeks.
guide.Regulatory: For pharma: a USFDA warning letter or import alert is a big negative, while a Form 483 with a few procedural observations (Dr Reddy's) is usually minor. Approvals, certifications and cuts in tax demands (Paytm) are positives; new or higher tax demands (Mphasis) and lawsuits (Bank of Baroda) are negatives, though most are disputed for years. Rule changes by NPCI, SEBI or the exchanges (UPI fees, F&O exits) can move a whole group of stocks.
guide.Management change: A sudden exit of a CEO or CFO can spook investors; a planned succession usually doesn't.
guide.Corporate action: Takeovers, open offers and delisting plans. These change who owns the company and can create short-term price moves. If the share already trades above the deal price (IDBI Bank), the upside depends on the open-offer terms.
guide.Fund raise: Debt or government loans don't dilute shareholders. Equity raises (QIP, rights, preferential issue) add new shares and can weigh on the price.
guide.Legal claim: A lawsuit or legal claim against a company. A big headline number can hit the share for days, but most claims take years and are often dismissed or settled for far less. Watch whether the court admits the case and what the company files.
guide.Rating change: Credit rating changes. An upgrade lowers borrowing costs; the share usually reacts within 1–2 weeks.
guide.Product launch: A new product or launch adds revenue over time; it matters most when large versus the company's sales.

items.title: US–Iran after the midterms: big strike threat vs talks
items.latest: 12 Nov: Iran said four tankers hit mines near Hormuz; Houthis attacked Saudi oil sites; Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran. Brent +3.3% to $95.82.
items.effect: A deal or de-escalation keeps oil low — strongly positive for India (rupee, inflation, OMCs, paints, airlines). A large US strike would send oil back above $100 and hit those same stocks; gold and upstream oil would gain.
items.when: Any day; Iran's response via Qatar this week
items.likely: De-escalation now more likely; deal terms still unresolved
items.watch: Formal talks via Qatar; any Hormuz incident; Brent back above $100

items.title: Ethanol/biofuel plan scaled back after monsoon shortfall
items.latest: Per Kotak Neo's 4 Nov market report, a sharp monsoon shortfall has disrupted India's biofuel plans and the government is prioritising food availability over ethanol production. No quota numbers confirmed.
items.effect: Lower ethanol diversion would cut volumes and earnings for sugar-ethanol makers; may also slow blending targets for OMCs.
items.when: Ethanol supply year allocations (timing not confirmed)

items.title: Coal India to list Mahanadi Coalfields (~$1 bn IPO)
items.latest: 3 Nov: Coal India plans an IPO of about $1 bn for its Mahanadi Coalfields subsidiary in November or early December (Kotak Neo).
items.effect: Unlocks value for Coal India shareholders and adds to disinvestment receipts; a big IPO can briefly draw money from other PSU stocks.
items.likely: Medium-high: timeline given, price and size not final
items.watch: DRHP/RHP filing, price band, anchor book

items.title: India–US trade deal
items.who: Commerce Ministry and US Trade Representative
items.latest: US envoy Sergio Gor said on 31 Oct the deal is 'at the finish line' but gave no date. On 2 Nov a White House list claimed the deal is 'secured', though only a February framework has been announced (The Tribune).
items.effect: A deal that lowers US tariffs would help exporters that depend on the US: textiles and apparel, gems and jewellery, auto parts, chemicals, seafood. Failure or new tariffs would hit the same group.
items.when: Announcement 'within weeks' per Rubio; leaders' signing could follow
items.likely: Likely in coming weeks; White House claim not confirmed by India
items.watch: Official signing date; tariff details for textiles, pharma, auto parts

items.title: US Fed: December rate hike risk
items.latest: Cleveland Fed's Hammack (12 Nov) backed smaller, more frequent hikes; CME prices a 25 bp December hike fully, ~13% odds of 50 bps. US 10-yr hit 5.10%.
items.effect: A December hike would lift the dollar and US yields, pressure the rupee and FII flows, and weigh on IT, banks and gold ETFs.
items.when: 9 Dec 2026 decision; US PCE (29 Oct), jobs and CPI data before that
items.watch: US PPI Fri 13 Nov, retail sales, Fed speakers; decision 9 Dec

items.title: RBI rate decision: another hike likely in December
items.latest: October CPI came in at 6.09% on 12 Nov (Sept 5.54%), above the 6% ceiling, with food inflation at 8.94%. Repo is 5.50% after the 7 Oct hike; minutes said cuts are off the table.
items.effect: A hike raises borrowing costs: negative for rate-sensitive stocks such as NBFCs, real estate and autos, and for bond prices. Banks can gain on margins at first. A pause would be a relief rally trigger.
items.likely: Hike looks likely — inflation is above the band and the Fed is set to hike too
items.watch: October CPI (12 Nov), liquidity operations, rupee and crude

items.title: OPEC+ oil output for December
items.latest: 1 Nov: OPEC+ core members kept December targets at about 31 mn bpd ('maintain September required production'). 1.65 mn bpd of 2023 cuts was fully unwound in September; 2 mn bpd of 2022 cuts stays through year-end. Brent settled at $117.64 on 30 Oct.
items.effect: Higher output would ease crude and help India's rupee, inflation and oil marketing companies. A cut would do the opposite.
items.watch: 29 Nov meeting on 2027 output; Hormuz flows

items.title: IDBI Bank sold to Fairfax (60.72% stake at ₹81/share)
items.latest: On 14 Oct the Cabinet approved Fairfax's ₹52,878 cr bid: the government sells 30.48% and LIC 30.24% at ₹81 a share. IDBI jumped 9% to ₹90.39 on 14 Oct, then fell 8.1% to ₹83.07 on 15 Oct. Fairfax reportedly plans to combine IDBI Bank, Digit Insurance and IIFL Capital into one group. On 16 Oct Business Standard reported Fairfax proposes contributing Digit Insurance and IIFL Capital to IDBI Bank; CSB Bank denied merger talks with IDBI. On 17–19 Oct IDBI reported Q2 profit down 39% to ₹2,205 cr (the year-ago figure had a one-off ₹1,699 cr NSDL gain).
items.effect: Largest privatisation since Air India and a boost to reform sentiment. For IDBI shareholders, the stock already trades above ₹81; open-offer terms for public shareholders are not yet announced, so chasing the jump is risky. Fairfax must merge or exit CSB Bank, where it owns 40%.
items.likely: High (approved); RBI fit-and-proper and CCI clearances still needed
items.watch: Open-offer price and size; RBI approval; government's plan to sell its remaining 15%

items.title: Scrap LTCG tax on shares (and possibly cut STT)
items.who: Proposed by SBI Research · Decision: Finance Ministry
items.latest: SBI Research (12 Oct) proposed scrapping long-term capital gains tax on equities, with a 2–3 year holding period, to stem FPI outflows of ₹3.04 lakh cr this year. On 14 Oct the Finance Minister said it is 'too early to comment' and announced no change. On 19 Oct, Bernstein said an LTCG cut alone won't bring back FPIs and cut its Nifty target to 25,000. On 3 Nov Business Standard cited hopes of an LTCG review for foreign investors as one reason for the rally and record FII buying.
items.effect: If done, a big positive for the whole market and for FPI flows; brokers, exchanges and AMCs would gain most. Current LTCG is 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25 lakh. A cut in STT on F&O (raised to 0.05% on futures in April) would mainly help brokers and BSE.
items.likely: Low to medium: equity LTCG brought in about ₹1.29 lakh cr, hard to give up with a ~4.5% fiscal deficit
items.watch: Pre-Budget consultations (Nov–Jan) and any Finance Ministry comment

items.title: SEBI closing auction for the final price
items.latest: SEBI finalised the rules on 15 Oct: a 10-minute closing auction from 3:30 to 3:40 PM on all trading days, index and stock derivatives trading until 3:45 PM (some expiring index contracts excepted), and expiring derivatives settled on the volume-weighted average price of the last 30 minutes. Kotak Neo (9 Nov) confirms the 10-minute closing auction and F&O expiry settlement rules start 7 Dec.
items.effect: Changes how the closing price is set. Mainly affects traders, index funds and exchanges; little effect on long-term holders. BSE was among today's top Nifty losers (−1.8%).
items.when: Most changes from 7 Dec 2026; limit/iceberg orders into the auction from 8 Feb 2027
items.watch: Exchange circulars and broker system changes

items.title: 0.4% UPI merchant fee on payments above ₹2,000
items.latest: 26 Oct: Paytm said the proposed UPI MDR framework could add about 2.5 bps to its payment-processing margin; it is not yet in results. On 13 Oct NPCI deferred the 0.4% fee on certain merchant payments above ₹2,000 until after Diwali.
items.effect: A fee on large UPI merchant payments would give payment companies a revenue source; small merchants would bear the cost. Positive for payment firms such as Paytm when it starts.
items.when: After Diwali (8 Nov); new date to be notified
items.watch: NPCI circular with the start date

items.title: More PSU stake sales (OFS) this year
items.latest: About ₹55,757 cr raised so far in FY27 from stake sales in 9 PSUs (including LIC and Coal India). With IDBI, receipts cross the ₹80,000 cr target for the first time in 8 years. The government may sell its residual IDBI stake in the market.
items.effect: An offer-for-sale (OFS) is usually priced at a discount, so the PSU stock often dips for a few days around the sale. Meeting the target can reduce pressure for further big sales this year.
items.when: Through March 2027; OFS dates are announced a day ahead
items.watch: OFS announcements on NSE/BSE (usually the evening before)

items.title: Union Budget 2027
items.latest: Preparations are under way. The LTCG/STT debate, disinvestment, capex and the fiscal deficit (~4.5% of GDP) will be the key themes.
items.effect: Tax changes on capital gains or STT, customs duty on gold, and capex plans can move whole sectors on the day.
items.watch: Pre-Budget meetings and leaks from December

items.title: RBI liquidity support as cash tightens
items.latest: 27 Oct: RBI ran variable-rate repo auctions, including a ₹1 lakh cr 7-day operation, after GST outflows and higher reserve needs cut surplus liquidity to about ₹50,000 cr. Call rate averaged 5.70% (5.48% a week earlier); a weak G-sec auction saw the cut-off rise 20 bps to 7.60%.
items.effect: More cash from RBI eases short-term rates; if tightness persists, banks’ and NBFCs’ funding costs rise and bond yields climb, a negative for rate-sensitive stocks.
items.when: Ongoing; month-end government spending and ₹35,400 cr of G-sec maturities may ease it
items.watch: Daily RBI money-market data, call rate vs repo 5.50%, 10-yr bond yield
